_comment: Model catalog for the audio.cpp adapter (server/src/models/audiocpp.ts). Data, not code, so adding a model is a JSON edit instead of a code change. Licence rule: an entry whose licence is not established is marked "commercial": "no" until it is. See docs/AUDIOCPP.md for the verified/unverified distinction.

stability_community.name: Stability AI Community License
stability_community.note: Free for commercial use below USD $1M annual revenue; above that an Enterprise licence is required. The GGUF conversion does not change the weights' licence.

models.name: Stable Audio 3.0 SFX (audio.cpp)
models.description: The same Stable Audio 3.0 Small SFX weights as the native model, run through audio.cpp's C++/ggml runtime from a quantised GGUF. Lower VRAM and no Python stack, at the cost of reloading the model on every generation.

models.name: Stable Audio 3.0 Small Music (audio.cpp)
models.description: Music-tuned sibling of the SFX model above, same stable_audio loader and GGUF repo, different fine-tune.

models.name: ACE-Step 1.5 Turbo (audio.cpp)
models.description: Lyrics-conditioned vocal music generation via a different loader family (ace_step) than Stable Audio. Turbo variant, distilled for few-step sampling. Set lyrics to sing a song instead of generating instrumental audio.

license.name: MIT License
license.note: MIT, and unusually clean for a music model. Commercial use permitted with no threshold. The project also states its training data was licensed, royalty-free, public-domain or synthetic, which is the question that actually bites with music generators — though that is a claim on the model card, not a term of the licence.

models.name: MiniMax Music 3 (audio.cpp)
models.description: Lyrics-conditioned text-to-music. Unlike every other entry here it loads a package, not one GGUF: --model takes the weights directory and audio.cpp resolves five components (condition encoder, language model, flow transformer, RVQ depth decoder, vocoder) plus tokenizer/config JSON from it. The component filenames are not ours to choose - the loader resolves them from the package spec compiled into the binary and checks they exist before parsing any option, so neither --session-option nor --load-option can redirect them. This entry mirrors audio.cpp 0.6.1's minimax_music3_q4_0 package exactly, including its mixed quantisation: q4_0 language model and transformer, q8_0 RVQ depth decoder. Defaults are the loader's own published values.

license.name: MiniMax-Music3 Community License
license.note: Commercial use is permitted but conditioned three ways: a revenue cap, a mandatory attribution notice in your product's UI, and safeguards if you offer it as a hosted service. Read it before you ship — the attribution duty in particular is easy to miss and easy to comply with.

catalog_extra.name: ACE-Step 1.5 Base (audio.cpp)
catalog_extra.description: Non-distilled sibling of the listed ACE-Step 1.5 Turbo: same ace_step loader, same GGUF repo, the base fine-tune instead of the few-step distillation. Slower per render - it wants real guidance and roughly 3x the steps - in exchange for the quality ceiling the turbo was distilled from. The shared ace_step advanced-params row caps num_inference_steps at 20, but that ceiling is the turbo's; the main Steps field passes through unclamped. Untested end-to-end through this adapter.

license.name: MIT License
license.note: MIT, and unusually clean for a music model. Commercial use permitted with no threshold. The project also states its training data was licensed, royalty-free, public-domain or synthetic, which is the question that actually bites with music generators — though that is a claim on the model card, not a term of the licence.

license.name: Apache License 2.0
license.note: Apache-2.0, per the upstream README and the license tag on the model repo, and corroborated by audio.cpp's conversion table. Marked conditional rather than yes because the LICENSE file itself could not be read, so the licence text has not been reviewed.

catalog_extra.name: HTDemucs stem separation (audio.cpp)
catalog_extra.description: Splits an existing sound into stems (vocals/drums/bass/other) via audio.cpp's --task sep and the htdemucs loader. Not a prompt-based generator - run it from a sound's "Split into stems" action. Output stem names/count are read back from whatever --out-dir contains rather than assumed, since this hasn't been run end-to-end yet.

license.name: MIT (code) / research-only (weights)
license.note: The Demucs repository is MIT, and that is what everyone repeats — including audio.cpp's conversion table and, until now, this catalog. But the MIT licence covers the code. Demucs' maintainer has stated plainly that it does not cover the pretrained weights, which are provided for scientific purposes only. Since the weights are the thing you download and run, it is treated here as non-commercial.

Two secondary labels that disagree with each other is not a licence. Treated as non-commercial until it is.
